title: Growth & Risk Brief: Qtr Outlook + Customer Ask Template
body:
Purpose: Single-page executive-facing template that combines quarterly customer recap language with a compact renewal-health snapshot and a prioritized ask list. Idea is to give account execs + sponsors exactly what they need for a 10-minute update and a follow-up email to the customer.

Audience: Customer Exec Sponsor, VP/Head of Product, CS leadership, Renewal Owner.

Tone: concise, outcomes-first, signals of risk + clear asks (timelines & owners). Avoid deep engineering detail; link to artifacts for drilldown.

---

1) One-line subject suggestions (pick one)
- Subject: Brief Q1 recap + 30-day ask from Redwood
- Subject: <Customer> Q1 usage highlights & renewal note

2) Quick email template (customer-facing)
Hi <Exec First Name>,

Quick recap of this quarter and a small ask to keep momentum. Highlights below and proposed next steps. Happy to walk through live — 15 min if helpful.

Top-line: 90% of API calls meet 95th pct latency target; embedding spend up 28% QoQ; early results from gen-qa pilot show 12% reduction in downstream moderation flags.

Wins:
- Production: 99.96% uptime for the deployed gen models; average token cost down 14% after batching tweaks.
- Product impact: Two high-value features (Search Re-rank + Draft Assist) crossed 10k monthly active users during the quarter.
- Support: Zero Sev1 incidents; one Sev2 mitigated within SLA via canary rollback.

Risks to flag:
- Renew/Finance: Current committed utilization is 62% of reserved capacity; if adoption stalls, renewal pricing trigger may require negotiation.
- Tech: Latency jitter for long-context requests (+90s tokens) on region-eu is recurring; mitigation plan underway.
- Resourcing: Customer engineering runway for integration items ends on 2025-03-15.

Renewal health (snapshot):
- Contract end: 2025-07-31
- Renewal health score: Yellow (risk 5/10)
- Primary drivers: Moderate usage growth; clustered latency issues in EU; outstanding delivery items x3 (integration + observability + SSO).

Asks (prioritized & owner):
1. Align on go/no-go for expanding Dedicated pool (opportunity to reduce unit cost) — Owner: Account Exec — Due: 2025-03-01
2. Approve extended engineering runway (4 weeks) for SSO + observability items — Owner: Customer PM — Due: 2025-02-28
3. Pilot extended KV caching on high-rpm routes (low-risk, measure cost delta) — Owner: Redwood Solutions Eng — Due: 2025-02-15

Attachments: performance-deck.pdf, usage-snapshot.csv, renewal-options-2up.pdf (links below)

Suggested call agenda for sponsor check-in (10 min):
- 0:00–01:00: One-sentence status
- 01:00–03:00: Key wins + topline metrics
- 03:00–06:00: Risks + immediate mitigation steps
- 06:00–08:00: Ask review and commitments
- 08:00–10:00: Next steps & owners

3) Internal QBR slide one-pager (copy into deck)
Title: <Customer> — Qtr Snapshot & 60-day Plan
Bullets:
- Usage & cost: MAU, API calls, $/1000 tokens, reserved utilization
- Reliability: uptime, sev count, average p95 latency
- Feature adoption: top 3 features by DAU
- Renewal: contract dates, health score, financial exposure
- Top 3 asks & owners

4) Renewal tracker row (single-line to copy to tracker)
Customer | Contract End | Health | Next Ask | Owner | Next Check-in
<Customer> | 2025-07-31 | Yellow (5/10) | Decide on Dedicated expansion | Priya Raman | 2025-02-26

5) Playbook snippets (what to do for each health color)
Green: Prep contract upsell options, schedule product showcase, prioritize cost-savings ops.
Yellow: Run three tactical mitigations (cache pilot, dedicated sizing review, SSO delivery plan), request executive alignment within 30 days.
Red: Pause expansion discussions, trigger escalation path to VP-CS and Solutions Eng, propose short-term credit/discount to cover migration pain.

6) Exec talking points (for CSM or AE)
- Lead with business outcomes (MAU, conversions, cost delta) not infra metrics.
- Be explicit about what you need from them (approve runway, prioritize SSO) and why — tie to revenue retention.
- Offer one measurable short-term win we can deliver in <14 days.

7) Follow-up cadence & template lines (after email)
- 48 hours: "Just following up on the brief — any questions or preferred time to sync?"
- 7 days: include performance deck and propose 15-min slot.

Notes & links for drilldown:
- Performance deck: https://drive.redwood/perf-decks/<customer>-q1.pdf
- Usage CSV: https://drive.redwood/usage/<customer>-q1.csv
- Technical postmortem (latency): https://confluence.redwood/incidents/latency-eu-q1

Draft checklist before sending customer email:
- Update renewal tracker row (owner + dates)
- Attach perf deck + usage snapshot + renewal options
- Confirm owners for asks and fill dates
- Run wording past Solutions Eng for feasibility checks

Quick tips for localizing for execs:
- Replace product-first bullets with metric-first lines for CFOs (cost, ARR impact).
- For CTOs, add one sentence on kernel-level mitigation and ETA.

---
Revision history: created 2024-11-05 by Priya Raman, updated 2025-02-20 with new renewal scoring rubric and pilot ask examples.
